pairs.rationale: The collectors’ question about the Teacher and the didrachmas is followed by Peter’s recorded Yes at the start of17:25. This identifies the question being answered,without independently establishing a payment history,another tax amount or the force of the later royal-tax analogy.

Jesus asks whether earthly kings collect toll or tribute from sons or strangers. The answer From strangers and the conclusion Then the sons are free supply the precise response and inference of this analogy,without reconstructing an administrative exemption or importing a different contribution amount.

The sons-free conclusion follows the answer From strangers to the preceding question about kings collecting from sons or strangers. The link identifies the expressed premise of the inference,without treating the analogy as an independently established temple-tax rule.

Pilate directs the party to go and make the tomb secure; the narrative then has them go,secure it,and seal the stone with the guard. This is the particular instruction’s narrated performance,without deciding whether You have a guard assigns new personnel or refers to an already available guard.
